correctness.rationale: Primitive cube-zero matrices over any quotient R_m have q²−1 nonzero nilpotent residues. Cayley–Hamilton and a unit minor make X³=0 equivalent to det X=(tr X)² and (tr X)³=0. Fixing residue, trace and determinant leaves q^{2(m−1)} lifts. For shallow valuation v, q^{8v} primitive lifts reduce modulo R_{s−3v} and yield the constant count (q²−1)q^{3s−2−ceil(s/3)}. Deep matrices contribute q^{4(s−ceil(s/3))}. Direct multiplication exhaustive checks verify all 14 configurations and each valuation stratum, including characteristic two, extension fields and integer quotients.

value.rationale: The first nonquadratic nilpotency-index stratum in finite matrix centralizers is a natural arithmetic invariant, requiring a cubic trace–determinant constraint absent from the existing square-zero census. The exact valuation plateau for all shallow layers, uniform in length, field size and mixed characteristic, is meaningful structural information, and the centralizer interpretation makes the count applicable to nilpotent commuting-matrix studies.
